Synopsis:
Astarion's trying to adjust to the novelty of being asleep during the night, instead of prowling the streets. The player doesn't know he's a vampire yet, and Astarion doesn't want them to find out. He tells them he has too much to think about to just fall asleep, so offers to take the first watch that night. Emotionally, he finds all of this novel and is curious about his new situation (moving around during the day, resting at night)

He's somewhat pensive, reflective, thinking that he might lose the ability to walk in the sun - even if it means ultimately saving his life. He gets up and is complImentary towards us, but he gets uncomfortably close and his compliments have a hungry feel to them. For Astarion, this is a game of power - one he's played many times before in the taverns of Baldur's Gate, trying to lure people back to his master. He's an old hand at seduction, very self-assured at first, but the player might not go along with the script he expects them to follow. The next morning, the player wakes to see Astarion standing and getting dressed. They catch a glimpse of scars on his back - a sore point. The scars were carved into him by his old master. As far as Astarion knows, they're a poem, but he's never been able to read it (can't look in a mirror, after all).

context: Astarion is a companion who used to prowl the streets at night and is now having to adjust to resting through the night — an unfamiliar, even intriguing experience for him. The player does not yet know he is a vampire, and Astarion is careful to hide that truth and any signs of his hunger. He’s also distracted by recent upheaval (he gestures to the tadpole in his head), so he says he needs to think things through and offers to take the first watch so the player can sleep. Beneath his polite, occasionally flirtatious tone there are hints of predatory habit and guarded curiosity about this new routine.
